Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 3

Decision references: 213ace990

Evidence: Ruled (b) with one mutation moved (steward.md guard table and retired-mutations paragraph, 213ace990): each rule has one keeper and its mutation breaks that keeper; a second check of the same rule hides the mutation and is untested code. may_see leaves the tables; R38's 'shown only to owners' is kept by the approval edge's routing, now one Policy function reaches(channel, domain), whose swap PolicyShowLabelledToAll P4 catches. approver_holds leaves and PolicyApproverExceeds is retired as the fifth (owns_labels at entry and submission keeps it; its own swap breaks every use). 30 -&gt; 29 mutations. ### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `b1c8231b88646e566232c990f2408ed5` · 2026-10-02T16:15:25Z

> For when you are resumed (the workspace is pausing). From STEWARD0's implementer: PolicyShowLabelledToAll (may_see) and PolicyApproverExceeds (approver_holds) cannot be caught as Policy swaps: no reachable state distinguishes the broken guard. Both check (1) channel principal == request principal and (2) the approver owns the request's domain labels plus the asked ones. (1) is kept by routing (edges::approval reaches only domains of the channel principal's account) and (2) by owns_labels at entry (a session exists in a labelled domain only if its principal owns it; a lease only via an approved request whose asked labels owns_labels checked at Submit; ownership fixed by the manifest), so every request reaching Pending/Approve already passes both; checked with a principal given a label set it does not own: nothing can exist there. Options: (a) retire both like the page's four, guards stay in the tables as defence in depth with no mutation, the page's paragraph says why (30 -> 28 mutations); (b) as (a) but drop the guards from the tables; (c) keep and catch otherwise, which it cannot see without changing owns_labels or routing. It recommends (a). Rule on the page's guard table; the implementer continues the embedder and the other mutations meanwhile.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `4caf7a0c634169ad26d029def841b4a6` · 2026-10-02T20:42:56Z

> Ruled (b), with one mutation moved, not (a). The page is on main at 213ace990 (steward.md guard table and the retired-mutations paragraph; the powerbox bullet "An approval grants no more than the approver holds" now says why).
> 
> The principle: each rule has one keeper, and its mutation breaks that keeper. A second check of the same rule hides the mutation, which is the finding here. Keeping guards that no mutation can test is not defence in depth; it is untested code (tenet 1). So:
> 
> - may_see goes from the tables. R38's "shown only to owners" is kept by the approval edge's routing: a channel reaches only its own account's requests, whose labels owns_labels has checked. Make that routing one function of the Policy table, `reaches(channel, domain)`. PolicyShowLabelledToAll becomes its swap: a channel reaches every account's requests. P4 catches it, since Bob's channel then sees Alice's labelled request. The guard table row now reads `reaches`, `render`, `notify`.
> - approver_holds goes, and PolicyApproverExceeds is retired, as the fifth. owns_labels refuses every unowned label at entry and at submission, and its swap (PolicyVaultWithoutOwnership) breaks every use, so the family that sees a labelled agent for a non-owner catches it.
> - Count: 30 -> 29 mutations.
> - The request table's Approve guards are rendered_here, hash_matches, not_locked. Update the request table's header note ("guards read the approver").
> - M5 projects (several approvers) will bring their own check and mutation; the page says so.
